newsitem.title: UK: UK funds seen buoying Halifax demand.
newsitem.headline: UK funds seen buoying Halifax demand.

text.p: UK fund managers joined in the scramble for shares in the Halifax Plc on Monday as they positioned themselves for the group's inclusion in the FTSE 100 index later in the month.
They said strong fund interest in the stock was likely to continue in the run-up to the June 23 changes to the index.
The Halifax will be in the top 10 of UK quoted companies.
"From a benchmark point of view they are going to have to have them and less than a quarter came through in the auction," said the head of UK equities at a British fund manager.

Index funds, which seek to mirror the composition and performance of indices, would be major buyers of the shares but demand would also be evident from active funds, a UK fund manager who asked not to be named said.
"For an active manager not to have Halifax in their portfolio would be a very significant position. They would not look to be overweight but that is not very likely anyway," he said.
Halifax shares opened at 774.5 pence but traded back below 750 pence at 1030 GMT.
